title: The roughness of a heartbeat through starved tissue
question: Within a source-ground-truth phantom regime transported to ISLES'24 patient support, does one frozen raw-temporal final-infarct surrogate respond selectively to flow-generated rather than technique-generated changes in Higuchi fractal dimension?
deliverable_original: The final-infarct model is using temporal fractal dimension of the raw contrast curve as a tissue-flow signal.
deliverable_sentence: One frozen raw-temporal final-infarct surrogate trained on ISLES'24 selectively uses FD-equivalent temporal roughness generated by flow rather than matched roughness generated by the modeled acquisition and preprocessing factors, within the validated phantom regime.
rung: Target rung 1 only: selective use by one self-trained surrogate within the validated perturbation regime. Replication in another architecture, cohort, acquisition pipeline, or challenge model is outside this card.
X_measurement: Compute voxelwise Higuchi fractal dimension (FD) from the released baseline-subtracted 4D CTP attenuation series using the frame-count-adapted kmax procedure reported by Ichikawa, Kondo, and Yokoyama (DOI 10.1007/s11548-025-03500-3; PMID 40824507). This is deterministic and requires no new annotation, but exact reproduction remains a Stage-0 gate because the authors' code is available only on request.
suspected_signal: Flow, transit and dispersion can change multiscale temporal roughness in a contrast curve, but the released series can also contain roughness from noise, motion correction, interpolation and one-frame-per-second resampling. The scientific uncertainty is whether a raw-temporal infarct surrogate treats FD-equivalent roughness preferentially as a flow-side cue rather than as generic technical texture.
keystone_prerequisite: Higuchi FD is computable and nondegenerate on released ISLES'24 4D CTP and varies across relevant tissue states.
keystone_evidence: Ichikawa, Kondo, and Yokoyama (DOI 10.1007/s11548-025-03500-3; PMID 40824507), inspected in the primary publisher and PubMed records: voxelwise FD was computed on all 149 public ISLES'24 CTP studies; it differed among core, penumbra and normal tissue (p<0.001), achieved AUC 0.732 for penumbra versus normal, and correlated with true CBF above 0.9 in the paper's phantom after kmax optimization.
keystone_residual_assumption: The inspected result proves measurement feasibility and association, not model use or physiological provenance. The exact recipe must reproduce, FD must remain decodable within CBF strata, and a source-ground-truth phantom must validate the flow-versus-technique generator before any patient-side source claim. Failure of any prerequisite is sensitivity-limited.
verified_dataset_facts: The published realized cohort is 245 adults from two centers: 149 public training cases and 96 hidden test cases (Riedel et al., Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2026, DOI 10.1148/ryai.250603).

Cases include acute pre-intervention NCCT, CTA and CTP; the public release contains co-registered 4D CTP temporally resampled to 1 frame/sec plus CBF, CBV, MTT and Tmax maps (DOI 10.1148/ryai.250603).

Final-infarct ground truth was derived from follow-up DWI acquired 2-9 days after successful reperfusion using DeepISLES followed by neuroradiologist-supervised correction (DOI 10.1148/ryai.250603; arXiv:2408.10966).

The 149-case training release is public via Zenodo under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with no DUA; the currently inspected release is a monolithic approximately 99 GB archive (Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.16731717; evidence/datasets.csv, verified 2026-08-18).

Official challenge measures are Dice, absolute lesion-volume difference, absolute lesion-count difference and lesion-wise F1; these evaluate segmentation, not the mechanistic intervention endpoint (official repository https://github.com/ezequieldlrosa/isles24; arXiv:2408.10966).
use_vs_association: Association is already published. Use requires one preregistered conjunction: (1) graded patient-support curve edits move measured FD while preserving area, peak height, peak time and the first two moments and pass the same support gate as unedited curves; (2) erasing within-CBF-stratum FD decodability from the frozen encoder changes output while preserving cross-validated decodability of CBF, the named moments, frame count and noise controls; and (3) source-ground-truth phantom validation shows that the frozen generator distinguishes flow-side from technique-side matched-Delta-FD families, after which the surrogate's patient-support response slope is larger for the flow-side family. Any single arm alone licenses only a weaker association or perturbation-family statement.
source_validation_gate: Before patient inference, independently inspect and acquire a primary-source digital CTP phantom. The proposed candidates are Kudo et al. (Radiology 2013, DOI 10.1148/radiol.12112618) and Manniesing et al. (PeerJ 2016, DOI 10.7717/peerj.2683; PMCID PMC5134368). Stage C0 must establish permitted use, known flow parameters, controllable temporal sampling and technical perturbations, patient-range coverage, and blinded recovery of source class and parameter change after an ISLES-like resampling/co-registration analog. The debate introduced these assets, but their sufficiency and transport were not independently reviewed; silence is not acceptance.
smallest_decisive_experiment: Freeze patient splits and one raw-temporal surrogate only after a feasibility memo specifies the model, performance gate and sample-size calculation. Reproduce FD; validate the source-labeled generator on a digital phantom; then, on untouched public cases, run four graded doses of moment-preserving FD edits, FD-selective representation erasure with matched random directions, and paired flow-side versus technique-side matched-Delta-FD perturbations. The primary confirmatory contrast is the within-voxel difference between flow-side and technique-side output dose-response slopes. All gates, tolerances, margins, case counts and stopping rules must be frozen before outputs are viewed.
standing_confounds_addressed: Patient-level frozen splits prevent voxel leakage. Within-CBF decodability prevents a vacuous FD direction when phantom FD-CBF correlation exceeds 0.9. Moment, frame-count and noise decodability gates address named correlates; random directions address generic representation damage; matched Delta-FD and common support address unequal perturbation dose. Phantom source labels address circular decomposition of already-processed patient curves. Residual limits remain: a finite phantom cannot represent every scanner, motion-correction, interpolation, partial-volume or AIF artifact, and transport to patient curves is an explicit regime-bounded assumption.
alternative_explanations: FD merely re-encodes CBF; within-CBF decodability and matched-flow controls test residual information but do not make FD biologically unique.

The surrogate responds to another roughness functional that co-moves with FD under every authorized edit; the positive claim therefore remains FD-equivalent roughness, not unique computation of the Higuchi formula.
A phantom omits a patient artifact that enters only one perturbation family; support-overlap and omitted-artifact sensitivity bound but cannot eliminate this transport risk.
Any encoder deletion changes predictions; activation-matched random directions and preserved control decodability test nonspecific damage.
anticipated_negative: If the surrogate passes held-out performance, FD is reproducible and decodable within CBF strata, all edit/support/preservation gates pass, the phantom generator recovers source labels blind, and the study is powered to a frozen equivalence margin, equivalent flow-side and technique-side response rejects selective tissue-flow use for this surrogate within the validated regime. It remains useful as evidence of a technical-roughness robustness hazard. A failed prerequisite, underpowered contrast, or non-equivalence null is sensitivity-limited and says nothing about model use.
dies_like_prior: This remains exposed to the charter's dominant IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE: fitted patient curves cannot provide true flow-versus-technique labels. It differs only if Stage C0 validates those labels prospectively in a source-ground-truth phantom and transport is explicitly bounded. It also remains exposed to DATA_ACCESS if the phantom, exact FD method, or a workable raw-temporal model cannot be obtained; no weakened conclusion is adopted inside this card if those gates fail.
closest_prior_work: Ichikawa, Kondo, and Yokoyama (PMID 40824507) measure the exact feature on the exact public cohort but do not test model use. Winder et al. (DOI 10.3389/fnins.2022.1009654; PMCID PMC9672821) compare concentration-time and residue-curve networks and inspect correlations with conventional maps but do not measure or erase FD. Klug et al. (PMID 32501132; PMCID PMC7922756) show that regional context improves tissue-outcome prediction using conventional perfusion information. Kudo et al. and Manniesing et al. provide candidate ground-truth simulation instruments, not an ISLES'24 model-use result. A targeted search found no source-selective FD use-test; that is not proof of novelty.
novelty_delta: The precise, limited-search delta is a causal model-behavior test that separates flow-generated from modeled technique-generated matched FD changes after descriptor-use gates; prior work establishes FD association, temporal modeling, or phantom generation separately.
existing_assets: Public 149-case ISLES'24 training archive and final masks; a published exact-cohort FD method; published raw-temporal model precedents; and two primary-source candidate digital phantoms. There is no verified reusable FD code, checkpoint, frozen source generator, or inspected patient-support transport procedure.
remaining_legwork: A feasibility memo must inspect phantom files and licenses, reproduce FD on a prespecified sample, verify archive extraction granularity, define the surrogate and frozen split, quantify patient/phantom support overlap, simulate omitted artifact families, perform a power analysis, and price CPU fitting plus model training. Current honest estimate is multiple stages, about 30 GPU-hours across roughly three sessions plus several CPU-days and approximately 100 GB of source storage; it is not a one-session probe.
entry_point_2_requirements: Measurement: voxelwise Higuchi FD. Confused sources: flow versus acquisition noise, temporal resampling, interpolation and motion-correction residue. Matched source-labeled phantom perturbations plus patient-support and representation-preservation gates are required.
annotation_burden: No new expert annotation is required. Existing final-infarct masks support model training and performance gating; phantom parameters supply source labels by construction.
prohibited_conclusions: that the surrogate explicitly computes the Higuchi algorithm
that FD has a unique biological interpretation
that unmodeled patient artifacts are excluded
that a challenge winner or another architecture uses the signal
that the signal improves clinical decisions or segmentation accuracy
that a failed prerequisite is evidence of non-use

clarity.why: The confirmatory contrast is one flow-versus-technique matched-dose slope difference, but it depends on a long prerequisite stack.

identifiability.why: Source-ground-truth validation directly targets the main alternative, but phantom-to-patient transport and omitted artifact families remain serious.

medical_relevance.why: Distinguishing physiological temporal cues from preprocessing texture matters for robustness, but the claim concerns one surrogate.

interest.why: A model selectively treating curve roughness as flow, or revealing it as a technical artifact, would be mechanistically informative.

prior_legwork.why: The exact-cohort measurement and candidate phantoms exist, but code, checkpoint, validated generator and transport study are not ready.

feasibility.why: The program needs phantom inspection and validation, FD reproduction, model training, power analysis and several compute stages; a sensitivity-limited stop is likely.

data_readiness.why: ISLES'24 is public but monolithic and large; phantom availability and allowed derived use still require independent inspection.

evaluation_readiness.why: Segmentation metrics exist, but the source-recovery, support, preservation and equivalence criteria are custom and not frozen.

negative_result_value.why: An equivalence-bounded null after every gate rejects selective flow-source use for the tested surrogate and identifies a robustness concern; most early stops are uninformative.

novelty_confidence.why: Primary neighbors were inspected and no duplicate was found in a targeted search, but the expanded source-selectivity literature has not been systematically audited.

regret.why: The exact-dataset association invites a use test, but retaining physiological provenance makes the final step substantially larger than the scouting premise.

unverified_claims: exact reproduction of the published FD procedure
obtainability and permitted derived use of a suitable digital phantom
adequacy of the proposed ISLES-like phantom processing analog
blinded recovery of source class and parameter change
phantom-to-patient feature and parameter support overlap
a raw-temporal surrogate passing a frozen held-out performance gate
within-CBF-stratum FD decodability and selective erasure
the precise novelty gap beyond the targeted neighbors
plain_pitch: The public stroke scans contain a brightness curve for every brain voxel. Its jaggedness may reflect blood flow, but it may also reflect noise and preprocessing. This study first uses a digital phantom, where the source is known, to create equal jaggedness changes from flow and from technical effects. Only if every measurement and realism gate passes does it ask whether one self-trained stroke surrogate responds more to the flow-made version. Equal responses would be a useful warning that the surrogate treats technical roughness like physiology.
